<STRUCT_0001>
Toric stacks provide a great class of examples and a natural testing ground
for conjectures due to the dictionary between the geometry of a toric stack
and the combinatorics of its stacky fan in a similar way that toric varieties
provide examples and counterexamples in scheme theory.
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> Borisov, Chen and Smith: <EMPHOPEN_0001>The orbifold Chow ring of toric
Deligne-Mumford stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0001> <REF_0001>
<STRUCT_0004>
Inspired by Cox's construction for toric varieties, this paper defines
smooth toric DM stacks as explicit quotient stacks associated to a
combinatorial object called a <EMPHOPEN_0002>stacky fan<EMPHCLOSE_0002>.
<STRUCT_0005>
<STRUCT_0006> Iwanari: <EMPHOPEN_0003>The category of toric stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0003> <REF_0002>
<STRUCT_0007>
This paper defines a <EMPHOPEN_0004>toric triple<EMPHCLOSE_0004> as a smooth Deligne-Mumford stack
<MATH_0001> with an open immersion <MATH_0002>
with dense image (and therefore <MATH_0003> is an orbifold) and an action
<MATH_0004>. It is shown that
there is an equivalence between the 2-category of toric triples and the
1-category of stacky fans. The relationship between toric triples and the
definition of smooth toric DM stacks in <REF_0003> is discussed.
<STRUCT_0008>
<STRUCT_0009> Iwanari: <EMPHOPEN_0005>Integral Chow rings for toric stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0005>
<REF_0004>
<STRUCT_0010>
Generalizes Cox's <MATH_0005>-collections for toric varieties to toric orbifolds.
<STRUCT_0011>
<STRUCT_0012> Perroni: <EMPHOPEN_0006>A note on toric Deligne-Mumford stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0006>
<REF_0005>
<STRUCT_0013>
Generalizes Cox's <MATH_0006>-collections and Iwanari's paper
<REF_0006> to general smooth toric DM stacks.
<STRUCT_0014>
<STRUCT_0015> Fantechi, Mann, and Nironi: <EMPHOPEN_0007>Smooth toric DM stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0007>
<REF_0007>
<STRUCT_0016>
This paper defines a smooth toric DM stack as a smooth DM stack
<MATH_0007> with the action of a DM torus <MATH_0008> (ie. a Picard
stack isomorphic to <MATH_0009> with <MATH_0010> finite) having an open dense
orbit isomorphic to <MATH_0011>. They give a ``bottom-up description''
and prove an equivalence between smooth toric DM stacks and stacky fans.
<STRUCT_0017>
<STRUCT_0018> Geraschenko and Satriano: <EMPHOPEN_0008>Toric Stacks I and II<EMPHCLOSE_0008>
<REF_0008> and <REF_0009>
<STRUCT_0019>
These papers define a toric stack as the stack quotient of a toric
variety by a subgroup of its torus. A generically stacky toric stack
is defined as a torus invariant substack of a toric stack. This definition
encompasses and extends previous definitions of toric stacks. The first
paper develops a dictionary between the combinatorics of stacky fans
and the geometry of the corresponding stacks. It also gives a moduli
interpretation of smooth toric stacks, generalizing the one in <REF_0010>.
The second paper proves an intrinsic characterization of toric stacks.
